text:
$AMZN gave plenty of warning technically on its mild rally attempt into mid-October, but the real warning was today's break to multi-month lows on above avg volume which happened ahead of tonight's post mkt gap-down

This hasn't proven too weak overall outside of short-term churning, & suspect June/July lows (where the stock is trading now) could act as support tomorrow ahead of a recovery attempt into Nov

However, similar to $GOOGL, i don't find buying dips all that attractive when met with huge high to low ranges on big volume.  They tend to normally be wave 3 moves and even on a mild recovery, i suspect mid-Nov into Nov expiration might prove tricky-  Nov 11-Nov 20 timeframe

Ultimately, many continue to fail to see the improvement in the broader mkt and are putting too much stock in this minor (granted, outsized) move in Tech these last couple weeks.   Did they forget what happened Mon-Wed of this week? 

Symmetrically, QQQ bottomed Fri 10/16, it bottomed Friday 10/23 and what does it do tomorrow, 10/23? ____
Breadth & positive divergence are key.   Stay tuned.

@IBDinvestors @Marketsurge charts by #IBD show great clarity on this minor rally failure & breakdown.  but ultimately should prove short-lived.

Notes Josh recently recommended $RDDT which fell from $106 after hours by 21% or $28, and about $100 over ten weeks, with no contrition or pushback on CNBC.
text:
Drawdown Josh Brown's bullish, confident and remarkably simplistic soliloquy on technology earnings and stock prices this week (below) summarizes what is so wrong with Fin TV and the business media.

The investment mosaic is so much more complex than his 'glittering generalities' and singular factor views.   

Here are excerpts from his comments earlier this week on technology earnings and stock prices. @CNBC @cnbchalftime:

"Earnings expectations for tech are not coming down they are going higher.
We have an anti-bubble in technology.
When you think about the type of earnings we are going to get! 
We are going to hear from Amazon $AMZN on Thursday after the close - it could be explosive." 

Here is the full tape:
(2) Martin Pelletier on X: "Ouch. https://x.com/_Investinq/status/2115205675978834222/video/1" / X   

As I mentioned, Josh recently brought $RDDT (-$28 to $106 or -21% in after hours and -$100 in the last ten weeks or so since he recommended the name.  

@CNBC viewers have not heard any contrition and there has been no pushback by @CNBC moderator(s).

Unfortunately these are two big mistakes are not in isolation. 

I recognize that this tweet sounds ad hominem.  

I see my role is being an advocate to the retail consumer/viewer @cnbc and I am simply bringing up the facts by reiterating what he said.

If anyone at @CNBC or elsewhere on Twitter feel I am in attack mode, tell me and explain.  Unlike some, I can always learn... 

@KeithMcCullough @Hedgeye_HGRO @RPKInve

text:
$AMZN CEO Andy Jassy argues that the scale and pace of the AI opportunity justify aggressive upfront CapEx, despite the pressure on near-term FCF

“...he way we think about it....is that this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity....Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years? And you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient. But that's not the world that we live in. And that's not the opportunity.

"And we can fund this plan, and I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change—it will forever change—our revenue. It will forever change our free cash flow. And we're going to invest and we're going to pursue it to continue to be the significant leader like we are today."
